scope: Entrepreneurship in the health sector for Applied Health Sciences students (laboratory, imaging and other programmes): whether business concepts are correct and applied to health ventures, whether every statement about a real Egyptian entrepreneur, company or programme is accurate and sourced, whether regulation and ethics are handled correctly, and whether every business calculation is right.
criteria: Each entrepreneurship concept (definitions, characteristics, types, stages, EDPs, ecosystem) is defined correctly and matches standard entrepreneurship texts.
The task and general environment, barriers to entry, outsourcing and Hofstede's dimensions are explained correctly and applied to health organisations without stereotyping any national culture.
Every concept is applied to health ventures, with realistic examples from laboratories, imaging centres, hospitals, pharmacies, devices or digital health.
Every fact about a named Egyptian entrepreneur or company (founder, year, service, funding, size) is supported by its cited source and dated; nothing is invented or promotional.
Statements about Egyptian licensing and regulation (EDA, Ministry of Health, radiation protection, Law 151/2020, Law 82/2002) are current and attributed to the responsible authority.
Need statements, personas, empathy maps, MVPs and the Business Model Canvas are built correctly in the worked examples.
Every start-up cost, price, contribution margin, break-even point, cash-runway, equity and valuation calculation is correct, carries its unit and is read with the right decision rule.
Patients are protected in every example: safety, privacy, informed consent and honest communication come before growth.
Perspective boxes for the laboratory and imaging programmes are accurate for those professions and balanced between them.
exclusions: Do not request advanced corporate finance, econometrics or legal drafting beyond an introductory course.
Do not request business plans that promote named commercial products.
evidence_expectations: Quote the exact text and give file and line for every finding.
Recompute any number challenged, and show the recomputation.
For a fact about a named person or company, say what the cited source supports and what it does not.
Give replacement text, not only a critique.
Cite a standard entrepreneurship text, or the regulator's document, for any corrected definition or rule.
